editorial_article: "1/2," frequently referred to by fans and critics as "Cliffs," is the opening movement of Aphex Twin’s seminal 1994 double album, *Selected Ambient Works Volume II*. Representing a significant departure from the rhythmic, acid-driven intensity of his earlier work, this track establishes the atmospheric, textural, and often unsettling sonic palette that defines the album. Like much of the record, the track is untitled on the original release, identified only by a circular chart of visual icons printed on the album sleeve. This "Cliffs" moniker was derived by fans from the corresponding icon, and has since become the primary identifier in cultural discussions of the work. \n\nMusically, the track is characterized by a sweeping, melancholic melody that feels at once expansive and claustrophobic. It eschews traditional drum patterns for layered, synthesized soundscapes that evoke landscapes—shifting, eroded, and alien. By utilizing microtonal tuning and dense harmonic structures, Richard D. James created a piece that feels caught between eras, serving as a landmark in the evolution of intelligent dance music (IDM) and ambient techno. The track is essential for understanding the transition of electronic music from the dance floor to the headphone-listening, contemplative sphere. It sets the tone for an album that continues to be cited as a pinnacle of electronic sound design, influencing generations of ambient and experimental producers who prioritize timbre and mood over traditional structural tropes. Its lasting impact lies in this ability to exist as a singular, immersive environment, detached from standard song structures and instead operating through a sense of sustained, emotive gravity.
